batch_strategy: Use matched response curves for m96, m92-EA, m186, and m25, alongside basic heteroaromatic, donor-geometry, loading-sensitive, and compact-control measurements. The batch emphasizes localized V2 tail boundaries and independent V1/V2 correction learning.

choices.reason: High-ratio m101 with a small sample volume probes ratio-loading interaction in a broad predicted endpoint region, complementing measured m101 contrasts 382c90a40989c39ceed1 and 987027dd660186de8266.
This high-width 10/1 condition tests whether a strong-ratio completion tail transfers across loading amount, informed by the measured tail-prone m39 condition f31a89256d8ee4192d55.

This intermediate m96 ratio point fills the response curve between compact and delayed measured m96 conditions 93ce299d2e2f5bf83250 and 376ba323d8d487f80cee, separating onset from completion movement.
The lower-ratio m96 point tests whether the predicted completion transition begins before the stronger-solvent region represented by measured m96 point 376ba323d8d487f80cee.
This m96 condition changes sample volume within the same tail-prone scaffold, testing the loading interaction suggested by measured m96 endpoint separation in 376ba323d8d487f80cee.
The 50/1 m96 point extends the ratio curve into a broad predicted endpoint regime and tests whether completion saturates or switches after the measured 20/1 condition.
Low-ratio m92 in EA anchors the solvent-specific endpoint surface near its compact side and complements the measured EA control 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b.
The 10/1 m92 EA point samples the middle of the solvent-specific ratio response, complementing measured EA outcomes e2f15590b7142490599b and 4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b.
This 20/1 m92 EA point tests whether the endpoint curve remains smooth after the intermediate-ratio region where measured V2 residuals changed direction.
The high-ratio m92 EA point probes the upper endpoint branch and extends the measured EA behavior represented by 7caf1db075b91197ba34 and 1844eab177de5d01fab6.

This pyridyl aromatic condition tests a basic heteroaromatic scaffold at moderate ratio and ordinary loading, bridging compact measured control a185774933bd6bb12c07 and delayed nitrogen-containing rows.
Low-ratio m211 provides a ring-nitrogen control with weaker eluent conditions and smaller sample volume, helping separate scaffold-wide basicity from ratio-dependent delay.

This low-ratio m90 point tests onset and completion near the lower boundary of the ester-bearing basic heteroaromatic region, complementing measured m90 points 0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c and 22f82413c75481d74e9b.
The low-ratio fused m146 control tests whether fused-ring nitrogen shifts onset independently of completion, complementing delayed measured m146 condition 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12.
This m186 phenolic aldehyde point adds a lower-strength donor-geometry reference to the measured m186 series, including 4a54ee0e355066ed7429 and 79faae5899539a97f8d9.
This donor-free halogenated aldehyde control tests whether acceptor and heavy-atom corrections transfer without a phenolic donor, complementing measured acceptor-rich endpoint contrasts.
The high-ratio m186 point extends the phenolic donor curve and tests whether completion broadening continues after measured 10/1 and 20/1 points 79faae5899539a97f8d9 and 1723e818bb3500feacec.
This broad high-ratio candidate tests whether a donor-containing or adsorption-sensitive neighborhood develops a completion tail under stronger solvent and larger loading.
This lower-ratio control provides a compact comparison for the high-width donor-sensitive region and can distinguish a baseline structural effect from a ratio-specific tail.
This m25 5/1 point samples the predicted boundary between compact measured 2/1 condition 075248a5ddcd4b5d091f and delayed measured 50/1 condition 3fc05dc2025715e68174.
The m25 10/1 companion tests whether the completion tail turns on gradually or abruptly between measured m25 conditions 075248a5ddcd4b5d091f and 3fc05dc2025715e68174.
This high-ratio donor-free aromatic aldehyde has a broad predicted interval and tests transfer from strong-ratio carbonyl behavior such as measured condition 4e01f3a3b2efd49f7fbc.
The companion small-volume condition tests whether the broad high-ratio endpoint prediction is molecular or instead depends on sample loading.
This donor-free aromatic ketone is a compact calibration anchor at 10/1 DCM, constraining correction spread from carbonyl and donor-containing tail regions.

A low-strength heavy-atom control supplies a compact nonpolar reference against delayed nitrogen and carbonyl neighborhoods, complementing measured m149 controls 822acada514c54d41f68 and 72f4152617833b191b9a.
This fused aromatic ether condition tests whether fused ethers remain compact at moderate ratio, complementing measured m124 conditions 55d368396013c3c895c3 and 39d0c96038ee0c9dace.
The low-ratio m22 ester point provides an ordinary acceptor-rich onset and completion control against measured compact m22 condition e560cf5c39e34dd9e4ae.
This ordinary ester condition at stronger PE ratio tests whether high-ratio corrections remain localized to tail-prone scaffolds rather than spreading across acceptor-rich rows.
Aminobenzonitrile supplies a donor-and-acceptor control without ring nitrogen, helping separate basic heteroaromatic effects from generic nitrogen-containing polarity.
This fused nitrogen-containing candidate expands the basic heteroaromatic region at moderate ratio and tests transfer from measured m146, m90, and m66 failures.
Naphthalene is a donor-free fused-ring control at 10/1 DCM, limiting spread of donor and nitrogen corrections into ordinary fused hydrocarbons.

This heavily halogenated donor-free aromatic tests whether mass and halogenation alone produce a completion tail, complementing measured compact heavy-atom evidence f62720d3fc5dbb0e173d and e514cee27f046099a732.

hypotheses.content: Completion tails are localized to scaffold, solvent ratio, and loading neighborhoods; similarly predicted structures can occupy very different V2 endpoint regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Localized completion corrections should improve tail regions without degrading the larger ordinary subset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched ratio curves show scaffold-specific thresholds, or smooth growth after accounting for loading?

hypotheses.content: EA-loaded m92 conditions are a promising solvent-specific endpoint region whose ratio and loading response should be learned separately from DCM behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: EA rows may otherwise inherit an inappropriate DCM polarity correction, especially for V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the EA endpoint mainly ratio-driven, or do amount and loading-solvent volume create separate branches?

hypotheses.content: Basic or ring-nitrogen-containing aromatic scaffolds can enter delayed onset and completion regimes that are not predictable from neutral carbonyl or ester analogues alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Basic heteroaromatics remain a coherent high-loss region and need controls that separate ring nitrogen from neighboring functional groups.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are delayed labels driven mainly by ring nitrogen, neighboring carbonyl or ester groups, or their ratio-loading interaction?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic and fused-ring structures separate into geometry-specific adsorption regimes; donor count alone does not determine delayed onset or completion.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Geometry controls can prevent the model from learning one generic HBD penalty and improve transfer across donor-containing scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor geometries remain compact at low ratio and which develop completion tails after a ratio or loading threshold?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, sample volume, and loading-solvent volume interact with ratio in tail-prone scaffolds, with V2 often more sensitive than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts teach whether corrections should act on onset, completion, or interval width.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are loading effects reproducible within each scaffold or restricted to particular ratio and loading-solvent cells?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl, nitro, ester, and related acceptor-rich families can show condition-dependent V1 changes that are not proportional to V2 changes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separate onset and completion corrections should reduce transfer of V2-tail residuals into V1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which functional-group and ratio combinations cause an onset threshold while completion remains locally smooth?

hypotheses.content: Many donor-free hydrophobic, heavy-atom, and simple aromatic ether structures remain relatively compact across ordinary conditions, but strong ratio or heavy atoms alone do not guarantee compactness.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Compact anchors constrain correction spread and protect calibration over ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-free fused, ether, and heavy-atom structures remain compact at high ratio and which acquire scaffold-specific tails?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes reinforced localized completion failures and separated V1/V2 behavior. The m96 and EA candidate neighborhoods motivate response curves, while measured m177, m159, m205, and basic heteroaromatic examples confirm chemically coherent delayed regions. Compact m12, m132, m139, and m9 controls argue against a global broadening correction. The batch therefore combines matched curves with low-risk donor-free and heavy-atom controls.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local ratio and loading curves, an EA-specific condition surface, basic heteroaromatic controls, donor-geometry tests, and compact anchors. The matched curves discriminate smooth response from scaffold-specific switching and separate onset corrections from completion corrections. Compact controls constrain overgeneralization from rare delayed rows, improving expected generalization across both high-loss tail neighborhoods and the larger ordinary portion of the Row-distribution.
